newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends softer but techs rally pre-Thanksgiving.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends softer but techs rally pre-Thanksgiving.

text.p: The Dow industrials extended their losses in quiet pre-Thanksgiving holiday trading, although the overall market was buoyed by renewed vigor in the high-technology sector.
"The buzzword is: Intel and Microsoft. It's the same names and we have a broad-based chip rally. It's the only area doing really well today," said Scott Bleier of Prime Charter Ltd.
The Dow industrials slumped 29 points to about 6499, the biggest point loss so far in November.
U.S. financial markets are closed Thursday for the holiday.
The Dow's losses were paced by Disney, off 2-1/4 to 74, after a Dean Witter downgrade on price. The stocks rose 2-3/4 Tuesday on its strong quarterly earnings report.

Also weighing on the blue chip index was profit-taking in the oil components, with Texaco off two to 98-7/8, Exxon off one to 93-7/8, Chevron, off 1-1/2 to 66-5/8, and Conoco parent DuPont, off 1-1/8 to 93-3/4.

NYMEX crude was firmer, with the January futures contract up 13 cents to $23.75 a barrel. OPEC ministers started their winter conference on Wednesday in Vienna looking to set production levels for at least the first half of 1997.
They are widely expected to roll over their current 25.03 million barrels per day ceiling. The meeting ends Thursday.
In the broader stock market, winners beat losers 13-11 on NYSE volume of about 377 million shares. The S&P 500 lost one to about 755.

But the tech-studded Nasdaq Composite rose six to 1287 as heavyweights Intel added 2-7/8 to 126-5/8 and Microsoft was up 1-3/4 to 155-1/2. It was the index's fourth consecutive record closing high. Among other techs, IBM inched up 1/8 to 158-1/8, Micron rose 1-1/8 to 33-1/4, Bay Network added 1-1/2 to 26-5/8 and McAfee Associates surged four to 49.

America Online added 2-1/4 to 34-7/8 after Cowen upgraded AOL to buy from neutral. Texas Instruments was up 2-3/4 to 63-3/4. Salomon upgraded TI to strong buy. The stock rose 4-3/8 Tuesday after news of a 10-year cross licensing pact with Samsung Electronics.

Michael Metz, Oppenheimer and Co's chief investment strategist, said tech buying was encouraged by the morning's economic data. "Inventory build-up was not as bad as previously thought. Durable goods showed capital spending would remain strong and that's bullish for technology."
The long bond rose 6/32 to yield 6.43 percent.

The morning's economic data included third-quarter Gross Domestic Product growth, which was revised to 2.0 percent against an expected 1.7 percent growth rate. Also reported was weekly jobless claims, unchanged at 342,000 and higher than the forecast 336,000 for the November 23 week.

Bonds pulled off highs after October durable goods rose 0.1 percent against an expected 2.0 percent drop. The Chicagoland Business Barometer rose to 57.6 in November against an expected 55.1 reading. "The data were pretty much in line, showing an economy growing at a reasonably slow pace with few signs of inflationary pressure," Metz said.

As for the overall stock market, Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter, said: "It's not over yet. Even though everyone likes to see a correction, it's just not happening here. The herd and the greed factor have taken over in the last few days. We know we are overvalued and we know we are up too much, but that's where the market stands."
The stock market will re-open on Friday for an abbreviated session, ending at 1300 EST/1800 GMT.
Among individual issues, Forrester Research, which provides products and services that gauge how technology affects business, surged six to 22 in its Wall Street debut.
Vacation Break rose six to 16-3/4 after agreeing to merge with Berkley Group, a privately held developer and marketer of timeshare resort properties in Florida and Virginia, in a stock transaction.
Smithkline Beecham rose 1-3/8 to 67-3/8 in U.S. trading amid rumors it will be taken over by Swiss drugs group Roche Holdings. Both companies declined comment.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 6.12 to 1287.32, a record.
The S&P 500 lost 0.96 to 755.00.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
-- Wall Street Desk 212-859-1721
